metadata.title: Drew Sample - Not targeted in Week 2
metadata.description: Sample notched zero targets during Sunday's 20-6 victory over the Texans.
metadata.analysis: Sample logged 36 snaps on offense in the win over Houston, finishing ahead of Erick All (25) and Mike Gesicki (21). However, after catching three passes in the 33-27 victory over the Buccaneers in Week 1, he wasn't targeted in Week 2. The 30-year-old veteran has spent his entire career with the Bengals since entering the NFL in 2019, most recently finishing the 2025 campaign with 15 catches (20 targets) for 106 yards and one touchdown. While Sample could find the end zone at some point this season, he's not expected to play a pivotal role on the receiving end. That likely won't change even if Gesicki or All aren't available, considering Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown should continue doing most of the heavy lifting on offense.

metadata.title: Drew Sample - Catches three passes Sunday
metadata.description: Sample caught all three of his targets for 19 yards during Sunday's 33-27 win versus the Buccaneers.
metadata.analysis: Sample was on the field for 42 of Cincinnati's 64 offensive snaps in Week 1, easily pacing Bengals tight ends in playing time. He has never been a truly explosive pass-catching threat, but a sustained high catch rate and regular playing time should keep him in the mix in a crowded passing attack.

metadata.title: Drew Sample - Finishes with 15 catches in 2025
metadata.description: Sample caught 15 of 20 targets for 106 yards and one touchdown and added a three-yard run during the 2025 regular season.
metadata.analysis: Sample played in all 17 regular-season games for a third consecutive campaign, all of which he finished with between 106 and 163 receiving yards. His three-year, $10.5 million contract with the Bengals runs through Sample's age-30 season in 2026.

metadata.title: Drew Sample - Cleared for Sunday
metadata.description: Sample (neck) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Sample upgraded to full participation after being limited in Wednesday's session, and the tight end is free of injury designation for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. The No. 3 tight end has been quite productive for his depth position in the Bengals' offense this season, logging nine receptions for 50 yards and a touchdown on 14 targets. Sample's health stabilizes a tight end room that might be without Noah Fant (ankle) for Sunday's contest.

metadata.title: Drew Sample - Limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Sample (neck) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: It's a new injury for Sample, who has appeared in all 14 games this season, including 11 starts. Sample doesn't do much other than block, as he's recorded just a 9-50-1 receiving line on 14 targets across 50 percent of the Bengals' offensive snaps.

metadata.title: Drew Sample sees two touches in Week 13
metadata.description: Drew Sample caught one of his two targets for 14 yards while also rushing once for three yards in the Bengals' 32-14 win over the Ravens in Week 13.
metadata.analysis: Sample remains minimally involved in the Cincinnati offense, finishing with two targets or less in each of his last nine games. The tight end can remain off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 14 contest against the Buffalo Bills.

metadata.title: Drew Sample - Blocker only
metadata.description: Sample played 38 offensive snaps (53 percent) Thursday night against the Steelers without a target or even a route run.
metadata.analysis: Sample has always been a block-first tight end, but this was an extreme result even for him. Then again, with Tanner Hudson out, the Bengals didn't have an alternative as a blocking tight end.

metadata.title: Drew Sample - More snaps forthcoming?
metadata.description: Sample had one catch while losing two yards on two targets in Sunday's loss to the Packers. He played 21 offensive snaps.
metadata.analysis: Sample could be in line for more playing time Thursday night, with Mike Gesicki (pectoral) out and Tanner Hudson in the concussion protocol. Sample's primary role is as a blocker, however, so that rise in playing time is unlikely to translate into bankable fantasy production.

metadata.title: Drew Sample - Cleared to play Week 6
metadata.description: Sample (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Packers, Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer reports.
metadata.analysis: Sample upgraded his practice participation throughout the week to gain clearance, as he went from a non-participant Wednesday to a limited participant Thursday before practicing without limitations Friday. Sample's impact in the passing game will likely remain limited, as Mike Gesicki and Noah Fant are ahead of him on the depth chart.

metadata.title: Drew Sample (ankle) off injury report for Sunday
metadata.description: Drew Sample (ankle) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers.
metadata.analysis: Sample will be available to play in Week 6, despite missing practice due to an ankle injury earlier in the week. He isn't expected to play a big role for Cincinnati in their matchup against the Packers, however.
